advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with a value carrying significant leading/trailing whitespace/newlines (e.g. "\n<pem>\n") asserting cfg.private_key is returned byte-for-byte, so a switch to raw.strip() regresses.
evidence: config.py:81-82 — 'Returned VERBATIM (not stripped) when it carries content — an OpenSSH PEM's internal newlines are significant'
config.py:108 — `return raw` (no strip), vs _str_env config.py:74 `return raw.strip()`
test file _DUMMY = "DUMMY-NOT-A-REAL-KEY" (no surrounding whitespace) and the only whitespace input '   ' is asserted to yield None — neither distinguishes verbatim-return from strip-return
advisory.finding: No test exercises the VERBATIM (not-stripped) contract for the inline PEM: _private_key_env returns the value un-stripped (unlike _str_env) because 'an OpenSSH PEM's internal newlines are significant', but every fixture uses a whitespace-free _DUMMY or a whitespace-only blank, so a regression that changed the return to raw.strip() (dropping significant leading/trailing newlines from a real PEM) would pass all tests.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: set _ENV to a value like "\n-----BEGIN...\n" and assert cfg.private_key == that exact string (unmodified).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard test_compose_still_works_after_pop with the project's _SSH_OK skipif (or shutil.which('ssh-keygen')) so it skips rather than errors where ssh-keygen is unavailable.
evidence: tests/unit/test_opcert_privkey_env_pop_932d.py:118-122 — subprocess.run(["ssh-keygen", ...], check=True, ...) with no skip guard on the test/module
tests/unit/test_extra_coverage_guard.py:19-20 — 'skips keyed on a missing binary or a version floor (ssh-keygen >= 8.9 ...) use pytest.mark.skipif'
tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py:66 and dozens of siblings all shell to ssh-keygen under `pytest.mark.skipif(not _SSH_OK, ...)`
advisory.finding: test_compose_still_works_after_pop shells out to ssh-keygen with check=True but has no ssh-keygen availability guard, deviating from the repo-wide convention (documented and applied in ~30 sibling opcert/identity tests) of gating such tests with pytest.mark.skipif(not _SSH_OK, ...); on a host where ssh-keygen is missing/too old this test raises a CalledProcessError/FileNotFoundError (build error) instead of skipping cleanly.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `@pytest.mark.skipif(not _SSH_OK, reason="ssh-keygen >= 8.9 required for SSHSIG")` (reusing the shared _SSH_OK probe) to test_compose_still_works_after_pop, matching the sibling opcert tests.
